# devicebasedauth.org

> Revocable, device-bound authentication and authorization as a pay-as-you-go web service. A device (browser, phone, server, CLI, AI agent) keeps its own private key; devicebasedauth.org issues it a signed, human-readable credential listing exactly what it may do, on which site, when and where. Servers verify offline for free or ask online (metered) for instant revocation, usage limits and owner approval. Prepaid balance, no subscription.

Machine-readable API: https://devicebasedauth.org/openapi.json
Credential format: https://github.com/curtcox/device-based-auth/blob/main/spec/credential.md
Grant evaluation rules and test vectors: https://github.com/curtcox/device-based-auth/blob/main/spec/evaluation.md
Revocation webhook events: https://github.com/curtcox/device-based-auth/blob/main/spec/events.md
Docs: https://devicebasedauth.org/docs/
Everything in one file (this summary, every route, the credential spec, evaluation rules and pricing): https://devicebasedauth.org/llms-full.txt
MCP endpoint: POST https://devicebasedauth.org/mcp (Streamable HTTP; Authorization: ApiKey dbak_… or a device credential)

## Key facts

- Money is integer micro-dollars (µ$; $1 = 1,000,000 µ$). Every JSON response includes `cost_microdollars`. `GET /api/v1/quote?op=<op>` prices an operation before you do it.
- Prices (µ$): issue 75, renew 25, online decision 10, metered API read 5, token exchange 5, OIDC login 10 (paid by the site), audience registration/change 100. Offline verification, JWKS, status lists, revocation, inspection and the web dashboard are free.
- Errors: `{ "error": "...", "code": "..." }` with HTTP status; 402 = insufficient balance.
- Private keys never leave the device. The service only ever sees public keys.

## Credentials

A credential is a compact JWS (ES256), header `{"typ":"dba-device+jwt","alg":"ES256","kid":…}`. Decode the middle segment (base64url JSON) to read it:
`iss`, `sub` (device id), `acct` (issuing account), `aud` (site names), `cid` (credential id), `jti`, `iat`/`nbf`/`exp`, `cnf.jkt` (device key thumbprint), `device`, `grants`, `status.status_list {idx, uri}`, `ver`.

A grant: `{ "actions": ["hashbin:content:write"], "resources": ["*"], "when": {"tz","windows":[{"days","from","to"}],"not_before","not_after"}, "where": {"source":"network|device|both","countries","regions","areas":[{"lat","lon","radius_m"}],"networks"}, "limits": {"uses":{"count","per"},"spend_usd_per_month"}, "require": {"online","step_up"} }`. Deny by default; any passing grant allows; unknown constraints deny.

Present it as `Authorization: DBA <credential>` plus `DPoP: <proof>` (RFC 9449 proof JWT signed by the device key with htm, htu, iat, jti, ath).

## Verify (relying party)

```js
import { createVerifier } from '@devicebasedauth/verify';
const dba = createVerifier({ audience: 'example.com' });
const result = await dba.verifyRequest(request, { action: 'example:write', resource: 'doc-1' });
if (!result.allow) return new Response(result.code, { status: result.status });
// Grants with usage limits / step-up / require.online: dba.verifyOnline(request, check) with createVerifier({ online: { apiKey } }).
```

Offline verification fetches `https://devicebasedauth.org/.well-known/jwks.json` and status lists (`https://status.devicebasedauth.org/v1/lists/<n>`, signed JWT, bit idx set = revoked), caching both.

Instant offline revocation: set `revocation_webhook` (https on your audience's domain) with `PATCH /api/v1/audiences/{name}`. Revocations of credentials naming your audience arrive as a POSTed JWS (`typ: dba-event+jwt`, signed with the issuer key); `await dba.handleEvent(await request.text())` verifies it and makes the verifier deny those credentials at once. Retried after 1 min, 10 min, 1 h; free for audiences; the status list stays authoritative. `POST /api/v1/audiences/{name}/webhook-test` sends a test event (read price).

## Enroll a device

- Browser: `import { DBA } from 'https://devicebasedauth.org/sdk/dba.js'; const dba = new DBA(); await dba.enroll({ aud: ['example.com'], grants: [{ actions: ['example:write'] }] }); await dba.fetch(url)`.
- CLI / agent: `dba enroll --aud example.com --action example:write` prints an approval URL for the human owner, then polls. `dba curl …`, `dba token --aud example.com`, `dba renew`, `dba revoke`. The CLI renews automatically at 2/3 of the lifetime when it uses the credential (`--no-renew` or `DBA_AUTO_RENEW=0` to stop); `dba renew --if-due` suits cron.
- HTTP: `POST /api/v1/enrollments {request}` where request is a JWS (typ `dba-enroll+jwt`, the new public key in the header `jwk`) over `{iat, aud, grants, device, lifetime_seconds?}`. Response: `approval_url` (give it to the human), `poll_url`. Poll `GET poll_url` until `status` is `approved` (then `credential` is included), `denied` or `expired`.
- Fleets: the owner creates an enrollment token (`POST /api/v1/enrollment-tokens {name, aud, grants, lifetime_seconds, max_uses, expires_in_days}` → `token: dbae_…`, shown once). Each device signs its usual enrollment request (aud/grants optional; may only narrow the token's) and sends `POST /api/v1/enrollments/redeem {request, enrollment_token}` — issued at once, issue price charged to the token's account. CLI: `DBA_ENROLLMENT_TOKEN=dbae_… dba enroll`; SDK: `dba.enroll({}, { enrollmentToken })`.
- Pre-approved issuance: `POST /api/v1/credentials {public_jwk, aud, grants, device, lifetime_seconds}` with an API key holding `credentials:issue` (or a device credential holding `dba:credentials:issue`, which can only delegate narrower grants).

## Main endpoints

- `GET /api/v1/whoami` — who is calling.
- `GET /api/v1/credentials`, `GET /api/v1/credentials/{cid}` (grants in plain English), `DELETE /api/v1/credentials/{cid}` (revoke), `GET /api/v1/credentials/{cid}/decisions`.
- `GET /api/v1/devices`, `POST /api/v1/devices/{id}/revoke`, `POST /api/v1/revoke-all {"confirm":"revoke-all"}`.
- `POST /api/v1/credentials/{cid}/renew` (device credential + DPoP; `new_key_proof` to rotate keys), `POST /api/v1/token {audience}` (≤10-minute bearer token), `POST /api/v1/self/revoke`.
- `POST /api/v1/authorize {credential, proof, request:{method,url}, audience, action, resource, context:{network}}` — online decision for an audience you own.
- `POST /api/v1/inspect {credential, check?}` — decode, verify, check revocation, evaluate. Free.
- `GET|POST /api/v1/audiences` — relying parties and their action catalogs (`GET /api/v1/audiences/{name}/usage`: your audience's online decisions, sign-ins and spend per month); register your domain (prove it with `https://<domain>/.well-known/devicebasedauth.json` = `{"account":"<your account>"}`).
- `GET /api/v1/account`, `GET /api/v1/transactions`, `GET /api/v1/audit`, `GET|PATCH /api/v1/account/settings` (dashboard only: `max_issues_per_day`, default 500; `max_renewals_per_credential_per_month`, default no cap; beyond them the API answers 429 `issuance_limit` / `renewal_limit` and charges nothing).
- OpenID Connect: `/.well-known/openid-configuration` (authorization code + PKCE S256; client_id = audience name).

## API keys and scopes

Create keys in the dashboard (`dbak_…`, shown once). Scopes: `account:read`, `transactions:read`, `credentials:read`, `credentials:issue`, `credentials:revoke`, `audiences:read`, `audiences:write`, `authorize`. Send `Authorization: ApiKey dbak_…`. Key reads are metered (5 µ$); dashboard reads are free.

## First-party audiences

`devicebasedauth.org` (namespace `dba`), `hashbin.org` (`hashbin:*`, mirrors hashbin's API key scopes, e.g. `hashbin:content:write`), `cronly.org` (`cronly:read`, `cronly:run`, `cronly:change`, `cronly:prose`, `cronly:secrets:write`). `<ns>:session` means "may sign in to that site".

---

# Every API route

Access: PUBLIC needs nothing; SESSION is the dashboard (Clerk session or a DBA browser credential); DEVICE is a device credential + DPoP proof; a scope means an API key with it (or a session, or a device credential holding dba:<scope>). Full schemas: https://devicebasedauth.org/openapi.json

- `GET /health` (public): Service health and deployed commit.
- `GET /.well-known/jwks.json` (public): Issuer public keys (JWKS).
- `GET /.well-known/openid-configuration` (public): OpenID Connect discovery document.
- `GET /status/v1/lists/{shard}` (public): A signed status list (IETF Token Status List). Bit idx = 1 means revoked.
- `GET /api/public/config` (public): Public configuration and prices.
- `GET /api/v1/quote` (public): Price of an operation (op = issue, renew, decision, read, token, login, audience).
- `POST /api/v1/inspect` (public): Decode and check a credential; optionally evaluate an action. Free.
- `POST /api/v1/enrollments` (public): Start an enrollment with a request JWS (typ dba-enroll+jwt) signed by the new device key. Returns the approval URL and a poll URL. Free; nothing is stored.
- `POST /api/v1/enrollments/describe` (public): Describe a pending enrollment ticket for the approval page. Free.
- `GET /api/v1/enrollments/{id}` (public): Poll an enrollment until it is approved, denied or expired.
- `POST /api/v1/enrollments/approve` (session): Approve an enrollment (optionally narrowing grants) and issue the credential. Charges the issue price.
- `POST /api/v1/enrollments/deny` (session): Deny an enrollment.
- `POST /api/v1/enrollments/redeem` (public): Enroll with an enrollment token instead of a per-device approval: body {request (the dba-enroll+jwt; aud and grants may be left out or narrow the token's), enrollment_token}. Charges the issue price to the token's account.
- `GET /api/v1/enrollment-tokens` (credentials:issue): Enrollment tokens (dbae_…): a pre-approved template (aud, grants, lifetime_seconds) for up to max_uses devices (1–10000) until expires_in_days (default 7, ≤ 90). The secret is shown once. Not available to delegating devices.
- `POST /api/v1/enrollment-tokens` (credentials:issue): Enrollment tokens (dbae_…): a pre-approved template (aud, grants, lifetime_seconds) for up to max_uses devices (1–10000) until expires_in_days (default 7, ≤ 90). The secret is shown once. Not available to delegating devices.
- `DELETE /api/v1/enrollment-tokens/{id}` (credentials:issue): Enrollment tokens (dbae_…): a pre-approved template (aud, grants, lifetime_seconds) for up to max_uses devices (1–10000) until expires_in_days (default 7, ≤ 90). The secret is shown once. Not available to delegating devices.
- `GET /api/v1/whoami` (authenticated): Who is calling: account, credential kind and (for devices) the grants in plain English.
- `GET /api/v1/account` (account:read): Balance, this month's spend and today's aggregated charges.
- `GET /api/v1/account/settings` (session): Budget guards: max_issues_per_day (default 500) and max_renewals_per_credential_per_month (default null, no cap). PATCH changes the members given; dashboard only.
- `PATCH /api/v1/account/settings` (session): Budget guards: max_issues_per_day (default 500) and max_renewals_per_credential_per_month (default null, no cap). PATCH changes the members given; dashboard only.
- `GET /api/v1/transactions` (transactions:read): Ledger, newest first.
- `GET /api/v1/audit` (transactions:read): Audit trail, newest first.
- `GET /api/v1/credentials` (credentials:read): List credentials (filters: status, audience, device).
- `POST /api/v1/credentials` (credentials:issue): Issue a credential for a public key you hold (API keys, sessions, or devices delegating narrower grants). Charges the issue price.
- `GET /api/v1/credentials/{cid}` (credentials:read): One credential: payload fields, grants in plain English, current JWS and history.
- `DELETE /api/v1/credentials/{cid}` (credentials:revoke): Revoke a credential (free, immediate online; status lists within a minute).
- `GET /api/v1/credentials/{cid}/decisions` (credentials:read): Online authorization decisions for a credential (kept 90 days).
- `POST /api/v1/credentials/{cid}/renew` (device): Renew the presented credential (same key), or rotate to a new key with new_key_proof. Device credential + DPoP.
- `GET /api/v1/devices` (credentials:read): Devices with their credentials.
- `GET /api/v1/devices/{id}` (credentials:read): One device.
- `POST /api/v1/devices/{id}/revoke` (credentials:revoke): Revoke every credential of a device.
- `POST /api/v1/revoke-all` (credentials:revoke): Revoke everything (optionally one audience). Body {"confirm":"revoke-all"}.
- `POST /api/v1/self/revoke` (device): A device revokes the credential it presents.
- `POST /api/v1/token` (device): Exchange the presented device credential for a ≤10-minute bearer access token for one audience. Charges the token price.
- `POST /api/v1/authorize` (authorize): Online authorization decision for an audience you own: revocation, usage limits, step-up, decision log. Charges the decision price.
- `GET /api/v1/step-ups` (session): Pending step-up approval requests.
- `POST /api/v1/step-ups/{id}/approve` (session): Approve or deny a step-up request.
- `POST /api/v1/step-ups/{id}/deny` (session): Approve or deny a step-up request.
- `GET /api/v1/audiences` (public): Audiences (relying parties): list, read, register (domain check, charges the audience price) and change. revocation_webhook (https on the audience domain, or null) receives signed credentials.revoked events (spec/events.md); it is only shown to the owner.
- `POST /api/v1/audiences` (audiences:write): Audiences (relying parties): list, read, register (domain check, charges the audience price) and change. revocation_webhook (https on the audience domain, or null) receives signed credentials.revoked events (spec/events.md); it is only shown to the owner.
- `GET /api/v1/audiences/{name}` (public): Audiences (relying parties): list, read, register (domain check, charges the audience price) and change. revocation_webhook (https on the audience domain, or null) receives signed credentials.revoked events (spec/events.md); it is only shown to the owner.
- `PATCH /api/v1/audiences/{name}` (audiences:write): Audiences (relying parties): list, read, register (domain check, charges the audience price) and change. revocation_webhook (https on the audience domain, or null) receives signed credentials.revoked events (spec/events.md); it is only shown to the owner.
- `GET /api/v1/audiences/{name}/usage` (audiences:read): Online decisions, sign-ins and spend per month for an audience you own (this month and up to 11 before it).
- `POST /api/v1/audiences/{name}/webhook-test` (audiences:write): Send a signed webhook.test event (typ dba-event+jwt, spec/events.md) to the audience's revocation_webhook now and report the answer. Charges the read price.
- `GET /api/v1/keys` (session): Account API keys (dbak_…). The secret is shown once.
- `POST /api/v1/keys` (session): Account API keys (dbak_…). The secret is shown once.
- `DELETE /api/v1/keys/{id}` (session): Account API keys (dbak_…). The secret is shown once.
- `POST /api/v1/payments/checkout` (session): Start a Stripe Checkout for prepaid credit. ?dry_run=1 shows the card fee.
- `POST /api/v1/dev/deposit` (session): Local development only: add credit.
- `GET /oauth/authorize` (public): OpenID Connect authorization endpoint (redirects to the consent page).
- `POST /oauth/authorize` (session): Consent page submission.
- `POST /oauth/token` (public): OpenID Connect token endpoint (authorization_code + PKCE S256).
- `GET /oauth/userinfo` (public): OpenID Connect userinfo.
- `POST /mcp` (authenticated): Model Context Protocol (Streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC).

---

<!-- Credential format: from spec/credential.md -->

# Device credential format, version 1

Status: draft (STATUS D2 recommends this format; implemented in `packages/verify`).
Conformance vectors: [`vectors/credentials.json`](https://github.com/curtcox/device-based-auth/blob/main/spec/vectors/credentials.json) (signatures),
[`vectors/evaluation.json`](https://github.com/curtcox/device-based-auth/blob/main/spec/vectors/evaluation.json) (grant evaluation; see
[evaluation.md](https://github.com/curtcox/device-based-auth/blob/main/spec/evaluation.md)).

The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD and MAY are used as in RFC 2119.

## 1. Overview

A **device credential** is a compact JWS (RFC 7515) signed by devicebasedauth.org with ES256
(ECDSA P-256, SHA-256, raw `r‖s` signature). Its payload is plain JSON that lists what one device
may do. The credential is bound to a key pair the device generated itself: every use is
accompanied by a **DPoP proof** (RFC 9449) signed with the device's private key. The issuer never
sees that private key.

Credentials are not secret, but they are useless without the private key. Anyone can read one by
base64url-decoding its middle segment.

## 2. Header

| Member | Value |
|--------|-------|
| `typ` | `dba-device+jwt` (credential) or `dba-access+jwt` (short-lived access token, §6) |
| `alg` | `ES256` — the only algorithm. Verifiers MUST reject anything else. |
| `kid` | Issuer key id; look it up in `https://devicebasedauth.org/.well-known/jwks.json`. |

## 3. Payload

| Claim | Required | Meaning |
|-------|----------|---------|
| `iss` | yes | `https://devicebasedauth.org` |
| `sub` | yes | Device id, `dev_` + 8–64 alphanumerics. Stable for a device key within an account. |
| `acct` | yes | The issuing devicebasedauth.org account. Relying parties map it to a local account (account linking). |
| `aud` | yes | Array of audience names (site domains) the credential is valid for. |
| `cid` | yes | Credential id, `crd_…`. Stable across renewals; revoking it revokes every version. |
| `jti` | yes | Unique id of this version, `<cid>.<version>`. |
| `iat`, `nbf`, `exp` | yes | NumericDate seconds. `exp > nbf`. Verifiers allow 60 s clock skew. |
| `cnf.jkt` | yes (device) | RFC 7638 SHA-256 thumbprint of the device public key. Absent on access tokens. |
| `device` | no | `{ name, kind, key_protection }` for display. `kind` ∈ `browser`, `phone`, `desktop`, `server`, `cli`, `agent`, `iot`, `other`. `key_protection` ∈ `webcrypto-nonextractable`, `secure-enclave`, `android-keystore`, `tpm`, `os-keychain`, `software`. Self-reported unless attested. |
| `grants` | yes | 1–32 grants; see [evaluation.md](https://github.com/curtcox/device-based-auth/blob/main/spec/evaluation.md). |
| `status.status_list` | yes | `{ idx, uri }` — the credential's bit in an IETF OAuth Token Status List. |
| `ver` | yes | Grant vocabulary version, `1`. |

Unknown top-level claims MUST be ignored. Unknown **grant** members MUST make that grant deny.

### Example

```json
{
  "iss": "https://devicebasedauth.org",
  "sub": "dev_7Q2M9X4K1B",
  "acct": "user_2abc",
  "aud": ["hashbin.org"],
  "cid": "crd_K3J8P1W6ZQ",
  "jti": "crd_K3J8P1W6ZQ.1",
  "iat": 1795017600, "nbf": 1795017600, "exp": 1797609600,
  "cnf": { "jkt": "0ZcOCORZNYy-DWpqq30jZyJGHTN0d2HglBV3uiguA4I" },
  "device": { "name": "Laptop — Firefox", "kind": "browser", "key_protection": "webcrypto-nonextractable" },
  "grants": [{
    "actions": ["hashbin:content:write"],
    "when": { "tz": "America/Chicago", "windows": [{ "days": ["mon","tue","wed","thu","fri"], "from": "08:00", "to": "18:00" }] },
    "where": { "source": "network", "countries": ["US"] },
    "limits": { "spend_usd_per_month": 5 }
  }],
  "status": { "status_list": { "idx": 48213, "uri": "https://status.devicebasedauth.org/v1/lists/7" } },
  "ver": 1
}
```

## 4. Presenting a credential

```
Authorization: DBA <credential>
DPoP: <proof>
```

The proof is a JWS with header `{ "typ": "dpop+jwt", "alg": "ES256", "jwk": <device public JWK> }`
and payload:

| Claim | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `jti` | Random, 8–128 characters, single use. |
| `htm` | HTTP method, upper case. |
| `htu` | Request URL without query or fragment: `scheme://host[:port]/path`. |
| `iat` | Seconds. Accepted from 120 s before to 60 s after the verifier's clock. |
| `ath` | base64url SHA-256 of the credential string. |
| `nonce` | Only when the verifier issued one. |
| `loc` | Optional device-reported location `{ lat, lon, acc_m, t }` (§5 of evaluation.md). |

## 5. Verification

A verifier MUST, in order:

1. Decode the JWS; require `typ`, `alg: ES256`, a known `kid`; verify the signature.
2. Require `iss`, structurally valid claims, its own audience in `aud`, and `nbf − 60 ≤ now < exp + 60`.
3. Verify the DPoP proof: signature by `header.jwk`; `jkt(header.jwk) == cnf.jkt`; `htm`, `htu`,
   `iat` window, `ath`; and `jti` not seen before (keep a replay cache for at least 3 minutes).
4. Check revocation: bit `idx` of the status list at `uri` must be 0. Status lists are themselves
   JWTs (`typ: statuslist+jwt`) signed by the issuer with `sub` equal to `uri`; cache them for at
   most their `ttl` (the service publishes 60 s; verifiers SHOULD cache ≤ 5 minutes).
5. Evaluate the grants for the requested action ([evaluation.md](https://github.com/curtcox/device-based-auth/blob/main/spec/evaluation.md)).

If the JWKS or status list cannot be fetched, verifiers MUST fail closed (deny).

## 6. Access tokens

`POST /api/v1/token` exchanges a credential + proof for a bearer token with `typ: dba-access+jwt`,
lifetime ≤ 10 minutes, one audience, the same grants, the same `status`, and no `cnf`. It is
presented as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and verified the same way minus step 3. Audiences MAY
refuse access tokens.

## 7. Status lists

Status lists follow the IETF OAuth Token Status List draft: 1 bit per credential, byte
`floor(idx / 8)`, bit `idx mod 8` (least significant first), zlib-compressed and base64url-encoded
in the `status_list.lst` claim with `bits: 1`. Revocations are published within 60 seconds.

## 8. Online authorization

Constraints that need state (`limits.uses`, `require.step_up`, `require.online`) cannot be checked
offline. Verifiers send those requests to `POST /api/v1/authorize` (metered, billed to the
audience's account), which also sees revocations instantly.

---

<!-- Grant evaluation: from spec/evaluation.md -->

# Grant evaluation, vocabulary version 1

Implemented by `evaluateGrants` in `packages/verify/src/grants.js`. Every implementation MUST
pass [`vectors/evaluation.json`](https://github.com/curtcox/device-based-auth/blob/main/spec/vectors/evaluation.json): for each case, evaluating `grants`
in `context` yields `expected.allow`, `expected.grant_index`, and per-grant `expected.reasons`.

## 1. Inputs

- `grants` — the credential's grant list.
- `action` — the action being attempted, e.g. `hashbin:content:write`.
- `resource` — optional, audience-defined string.
- `now` — the **verifier's** clock, in seconds. Device clocks are never trusted for time windows.
- `location.network` — what the verifier observed: `{ country, region, lat, lon, ip }`
  (on Cloudflare: `request.cf.country`, `` `${cf.country}-${cf.regionCode}` ``, `cf.latitude`,
  `cf.longitude`, `CF-Connecting-IP`).
- `location.device` — the `loc` claim from the verified DPoP proof: `{ lat, lon, acc_m, t }`.
- `online` — true only when devicebasedauth.org itself is evaluating (it can enforce counters).

## 2. Decision

The request is allowed when **at least one grant passes**. A grant passes when every check below
passes. Otherwise it is denied. Nothing is allowed by default.

Each failing check adds a reason code to that grant's reason list (all applicable reasons,
in the order of this document).

## 3. Grant members

A grant may contain only `actions`, `resources`, `when`, `where`, `limits`, `require`. Any other
member — at any nesting level listed here — makes the grant fail with
`unknown_constraint:<path>` and no other reasons. A grant that is otherwise invalid fails with
`invalid_grant`.

### 3.1 `actions` (required) → `action_not_granted`

1–64 patterns. A pattern is `namespace(:segment)*:last`, where `last` may be `*`. An exact pattern
matches only itself. `ns:a:*` matches any action starting with `ns:a:`. Namespaces are 1–32 of
`[a-z0-9-]`, segments 1–64 of `[a-z0-9_.-]`.

### 3.2 `resources` (default `["*"]`) → `resource_not_granted`

`*` matches anything, including no resource. `prefix*` matches resources starting with `prefix`.
Anything else is an exact match. An absent resource matches only `*`.

### 3.3 `when`

- `not_before` → `before_not_before` when `now < not_before`.
- `not_after` → `after_not_after` when `now ≥ not_after`.
- `windows` with `tz` (IANA zone) → `outside_time_window` unless `now`, converted to local
  weekday and minute in `tz`, is inside at least one window. A window is
  `{ days?, from, to }` (`days` ⊆ `sun…sat`, default all; `HH:MM`, `to` may be `24:00`).
  If `from < to`: inside when today ∈ days and `from ≤ time < to`.
  If `from > to` (overnight): inside when (today ∈ days and `time ≥ from`) or
  (yesterday ∈ days and `time < to`) — an overnight window belongs to the day it starts.

### 3.4 `where`

`source` is `network`, `device` or `both`; for `both`, the checks run independently against each
source and both must pass. For each source:

- Location absent → `location_unavailable:<source>`.
- Device location with `|now − t| > 300` → `location_stale:device`.
- **Places** (`countries`, `regions`, `areas`) form a union: the location must match at least one
  entry, otherwise `outside_location:<source>`.
  - Network: `countries` match `country`; `regions` (ISO 3166-2, `US-MO`) match `region`; `areas`
    match when the great-circle distance from `(lat, lon)` to the centre is ≤ `radius_m`.
  - Device: only `areas` are allowed, and match when `distance + acc_m ≤ radius_m` (accuracy is
    held against the device; a missing `acc_m` never matches).
- `networks` (network source only): the observed IP must be inside one CIDR range, otherwise
  `network_not_allowed`. Networks are checked in addition to places.

Location is evidence, not proof: network location can be moved with a VPN; device location is as
honest as the device. See the master plan §3.5.

### 3.5 `limits`

- `uses: { count, per }` (`per` ∈ `minute`, `hour`, `day`, `month` (30 days), `total`) — enforced
  only online by devicebasedauth.org with a counter per credential and grant. Fixed windows aligned
  to the Unix epoch.
- `spend_usd_per_month` — not checked by the evaluator. It is returned as a **caveat** for the
  audience to enforce on its own spending (e.g. hashbin's monthly spend limit).

### 3.6 `require`

- `online: true` — the grant may only be used through online authorization.
- `step_up: true` — online, and the account owner must approve each use.

### 3.7 Online-only constraints

If a grant would otherwise pass but has `limits.uses`, `require.online: true` or
`require.step_up: true`, and the evaluation is not online, it fails with `online_required` (and
the overall result reports `online_required: true` when that is the only reason any grant failed).

---

<!-- Prices and why: from docs/business/pricing.md -->

# devicebasedauth.org pricing and cost model

Status: **implemented; prices await owner approval (STATUS D6)**. Prices live only in
`src/utils/pricing.js`; rates and per-operation resource counts live only in
`src/utils/cost-policy.js`. `src/utils/pricing.test.js` fails if any price drops below its floor.
The public pricing page and `GET /api/public/config` read the same constants.

Rates are cronly's (checked 2026-11-15/16) and hashbin's price-floor sheet (2026-10-24). Operation
counts were taken by reading this repository's handlers on 2026-11-18; re-count them whenever a
handler adds a Durable Object call or a storage write.

## Rules

- Money is integer micro-dollars (µ$): $1 = 1,000,000 µ$.
- Prepaid balance, no subscription. $5 minimum credit, card fee itemized on top:
  `ceil((credit¢ + 30) / 0.971)` — a $5 credit costs $5.46. New accounts: at most $20 per payment
  in their first week. Credit is granted only by the verified Stripe webhook.
- A balance never goes negative: every charge checks funds in the same storage transaction.
  Issuance additionally checks funds **before** allocating a status index or signing.
- **Price-floor test:** `price × 0.92 ≥ 1.5 × ceil(worst-case marginal cost)` (0.92 = revenue kept
  after refunds/disputes; 1.5 = minimum margin). Included Cloudflare allowances are ignored.

## Unit rates (µ$)

| Resource | µ$ |
|----------|----|
| Worker request | 0.30 |
| Worker CPU ms | 0.02 |
| Durable Object request | 0.15 |
| DO row written | 1.00 |
| DO storage, per KB-month | 0.20 |
| R2 class A (write) | 4.50 |
| R2 class B (read, cache miss) | 0.36 |

## Prices and worst-case costs

| Operation | Who pays | Counted (per `OPERATIONS`) | Cost µ$ | Floor µ$ | **Price µ$** |
|-----------|----------|----------------------------|--------:|---------:|-------------:|
| Issue a credential (enrollment approval or API) | Issuing account | 3 Worker req, 19 DO req, 19 rows, 80 ms CPU, 6 KB × 13 months, 1 R2 write — includes a **prepaid revocation** and its webhook deliveries, and an enrollment token's check and use counter | 45 | 74 | **75** |
| Rotate a credential to a new key | Issuing account | Same as issue (new status index, old one revoked) | 45 | 74 | **75** |
| Renew (same key) | Issuing account | 1 Worker req, 5 DO req, 5 rows, 10 ms, 1 KB × 13 months | 9 | 15 | **25** |
| Online authorization decision | Audience owner | 1 Worker req, 4 DO req, 4 rows (balance, usage counter, decision row and its later deletion), 0.5 KB × 3 months | 6 | 10 | **10** |
| Metered API read (API key or non-dashboard device) | Caller | 1 Worker req, 3 DO req, 1 row (aggregated on the balance row) | 2 | 4 | **5** |
| Token exchange (≤10-minute bearer token) | Issuing account | 1 Worker req, 4 DO req, 1 row | 2 | 4 | **5** |
| OpenID Connect sign-in | The site (audience owner) | 2 Worker req, 7 DO req, 4 rows | 6 | 10 | **10** |
| Register or change an audience | Audience owner | 1 Worker req, 3 DO req, 5 rows, 4 KB × 13 months | 17 | 28 | **100** |
| Revocation, offline verification, JWKS, status lists, inspection, enrollment start/poll, dashboard reads | — | Free: prepaid, static, CDN-cached, or rate-limited and behind the cost brake | — | — | **0** |

Decision and login prices sit exactly at their floors (the thinnest margin the rule allows), and
issue is 1 µ$ above its floor since it prepays revocation webhooks and enrollment-token redemption.
Any upward correction found in an audit must raise those prices.

### Why aggregate small charges

A separate ledger row per read, decision or token would cost 1 µ$ each — as much as the operation.
These charges are summed into today's aggregate on the balance row (one write per charge, which the
balance update needs anyway) and flushed as one ledger row per kind when the day rolls over.

### Why issuance is the expensive operation

It carries 13 months of record storage and the full cost of revoking the credential later, so that
revocation is free and always possible, even at a zero balance. That includes telling up to 8
audiences by signed webhook (spec/events.md): four delivery rounds when an endpoint keeps failing.
The revocation shares one outbox row with its webhook deliveries, so the success path writes no
extra rows, and audiences without a webhook cost one registry lookup.

The webhook test button (`POST /api/v1/audiences/{name}/webhook-test`) is charged as a metered read:
1 Worker request, 3 DO requests, one signature and one outbound request.

## What customers would pay

| Scenario | Monthly cost |
|----------|-------------:|
| Developer: 5 devices, 30-day credentials renewed monthly | 5 × 25 µ$ = **$0.000125** |
| Small team: 200 devices, 7-day credentials | 200 × 4.3 × 25 µ$ ≈ **$0.02** |
| Agent fleet: 1,000 agents, 1-hour credentials, 24/7 | 1,000 × 720 × 25 µ$ = **$18.00** |
| Site doing 10 M online decisions | 10 M × 10 µ$ = **$100** |
| Script polling the API 1 M times | 1 M × 5 µ$ = **$5** |

A $5 deposit covers about 66,000 issuances, 200,000 renewals, or 500,000 online decisions.

## Margin and break-even

Margin per operation (`price × 0.92 − cost`): issue ≈ 24 µ$, renew ≈ 14 µ$, decision ≈ 3 µ$,
read/token ≈ 3 µ$, login ≈ 3 µ$. Profit = Σ margins − fixed costs, so it rises with every
operation (master plan principle 6).

Fixed costs specific to devicebasedauth.org, assuming the shared Cloudflare account and LLC (as for
cronly): the domain (~$11/year ≈ $0.92/month) plus Clerk if it ever exceeds 50,000 monthly retained
users. Break-even on $1/month is roughly 31,000 issuances, 71,000 renewals, or 330,000 online
decisions per month.

## Free paths and the cost brake

Free endpoints (`inspect`, enrollment start and describe) are marked `free: true` in `API_ROUTES`.
They write nothing (enrollment requests travel as signed tickets), are rate-limited per IP by the
`PUBLIC_LIMITER` binding, and return 503 when the cost-safety brake is on. The brake latches when a
day of measured Cloudflare cost × 30 exceeds `COST_SAFETY_BRAKE_CENTS` (default $25), or when
measurements are missing for 36 hours. Paid operations keep working: they are prepaid with margin.

## Open questions for the owner

1. Approve these prices (D6), or lower issue/renew towards their floors (74 / 15)?
2. Clerk monthly retained users are the one per-user cost not tied to an operation. Mitigations in
   place: dashboard sign-in with a DBA browser credential (no Clerk session). Proposed (D8, not
   built): close zero-balance accounts with no live credentials after 12 idle months.
